question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 765 through 774 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.
family: THE FAMILY FOR THIS BLOCK IS DECLARED BEFORE ANY CHAPTER EXISTS AND IT IS A WRITER'S, NOT A HUMAN'S. Somebody starts a job in their own place, somebody else arrives and takes the second half of it, and the second half is done quicker and better and in a way the host has never thought of. The host takes that way and uses it from then on, and the one thing the good way does not do is left standing where it was left. Ten chapters, five standing figures, the young man off the ring road sitting out because no second job is on the page, and in every chapter one job, one better way, and one fault that is in the better way and not in the host's. Nothing is measured, nothing is priced, nothing is added up, and no number is asked to agree with anything. The thing left at the end of a chapter is the one the good method was never able to do, and it is still there.
family_why_this_and_not_the_last_two: 0056 took a place-behaviour: someone comes as far as the edge of someone else's place and is kept there on purpose. 0057 took a task and a second pair of hands, two methods, one fault each, and it is the nearest of the three. **The difference is not the job and it is not the second person. In 755 to 764 the visitor's method was the one that was wrong and the host's own method was the one that got kept, and the host found something wrong with what the other had done. In 765 to 774 the visitor's method is right for the job and wrong for the place it is being done in, and it is the host's own way that is found wanting and thrown out. The thing left standing at the end of every chapter is not somebody's mistake. It is a hole in the best method available, discovered too late, kept because the method is better than anything the host has, and not repairable by going back.** A writer who takes a fault in the host's own work again has taken the last block's position and is repeating it.

family_tested_against_every_spent_family.595_604_small_thing_went_nowhere: Not this. Nothing here goes nowhere. Every chapter ends with the job done, done the good way, and visibly done, and the fault visible in it and left.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.605_614_carried_thing_could_not_put_down: Not this. Nothing is carried between people in the ten. Tools stay in the hands of the person holding them, and no object changes hands from one person to another, though a method does.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.615_624_told_thing_could_not_place: Not this. Nothing arrives as news needing placing. What is spoken is two people at one task in the place the task is in.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.625_634_decided_and_asked_why_and_gave_r: Not this, and this is the nearest of the two. Nobody in the ten is asked why and nobody gives a reason under asking. The trouble is not a decision and a defence of it. It is that a good method has a hole in it and the person who brought it cannot see the hole because they have never had to do the job any other way.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.635_644_brought_thing_and_had_to_lie: Not this. Nobody brings a thing for another and nobody says a false thing to spare anybody. The disagreements are out loud and honest and specific.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.645_654_woman_wrote_and_paper_left_house: Not this. No paper leaves any house in the ten. family_tested_against_every_spent_family.655_664_brush_carried_by_three_who_never: Not this. That was one object doing the work of three people who never met. Here two people meet on purpose, in the same place, at the same task, and they part at the end of it.

family_tested_against_every_spent_family.695_704_work_put_off_to_spring_with_ladd: Not this. Nothing is deferred to another season. Every job in the ten is done inside the chapter, well, and the badness of it is what is left.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.705_714_water_coming_and_bowl_emptied: Not this. The bath tap at twelve does not drip and the bowl is on its shelf with the ring on the tiles. Every job in the ten is dry work.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.715_724_call_to_house_where_person_is_no: Not this. There is no telephone in this block. No bell rings, no receiver is lifted, no message is left, and no line is put right. The machine and the telephone at twelve stand in the front room and are not touched.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.725_734_no_family_ten_scenes_each_standi: Not this. 0054 took none. This block takes one and the same one is in all ten.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.735_744_number_right_and_person_will_not: Not this, and this is the binding one. That family was a figure that does not agree with the thing it measures, and it is spent as a spread. No chapter here is built round a figure, a measurement, a tally of things, a quantity, a price, or a mismatch between a number and its object. A size is spoken in the prose because a job is described by hand and by eye and against a rule, and no number in the ten is an engine, a contradiction or anything a reader is asked to check.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.745_754_comes_to_the_edge_and_is_kept_th: Not this, and this is the second nearest. That family was a visitor at a boundary who was not brought past it. In 765 to 774 nobody is kept anywhere: the second person is put to work inside a minute of arriving, the argument is had over the work, and the host never sends anybody back to where they came from. Eight of the ten do have somebody arrive at a gate or a door, and the host in every one of the eight lets them in and keeps them there all morning. The departure gesture that stood in 0755 and 0764 is used once and not twice in this block, and a departure up a lane appears in only one of the ten.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.755_764_task_and_a_second_pair_of_hands_: Not this, and it is the nearest of them all, and the difference is stated in family_why_this_and_not_the_last_two. **Two faults, one each, in 755 to 764. One fault here, and it is in the method that is adopted.** In the ten of 765 to 774 the host's own way is the thing that gets found wanting and the visitor's way is the thing that gets kept, and that is the opposite of every chapter of 755 to 764, where the visitor's way was the fault and the host's own was what stayed. The two blocks share a shape and take opposite ends of it, and a later writer may not go back to two faults.

figure_rule_for_this_block: No engine with arithmetic. Ordinary domestic pairs (two stools, two hands, two turns of wire) appear as furniture in a few chapters and are not tallies and are not worked on. No measurement, price, room tally or mismatch is the engine of any chapter. Dimensions are spoken in the prose because a job is described by hand, by eye and against a rule, and no number in the ten is an engine, a contradiction or anything a reader is asked to check.
declared_ordinary_word_note: Declared in this file before any chapter of 765 to 774 existed and not after. It is not usually, anyway, like, just, enough, still, kind, quite, small, round, one, week, almost, anything, and then, nearly, away, count, garden, or shoulder, all of which are spent and none of which is re-declared.

bands.first_holding_order: Counted in chapter order: late forties at 0765, early thirties at 0766, seventy-eight at 0767, late fifties at 0768, early forties at 0769, then the same five again from 0770 in the same order. This block starts with the lock-up and runs the houses in the order lock-up, ten, twelve, nine, unit, and repeats that order. A writer of 775 onward may not take either order without saying so.**
bands.late_fifties: Stays at number nine alone, two chapters, 0768 and 0773. No early fifties and no late fifties figure is added to anybody.
bands.one_band_per_figure: Each of the five standing figures keeps one band for the whole block. bands.roster_rule: Every figure actually aged in a file is written down by eyes. 0765 late forties. 0766 early thirties. 0767 seventy-eight. 0768 late fifties. 0769 early forties. 0770 late forties. 0771 early thirties. 0772 seventy-eight. 0773 late fifties. 0774 early forties. bands.unaged_visitors: Three new unaged figures in ten chapters: the man who lives over the lock-up gate in 0770, the man from the end of the row at number ten in 0771, and the man who does odd work up the road at number nine in 0773. **The man in 0773 comes to the gate of nine with a canvas tool bag over his shoulder and takes a spanner out of it, and no shopping goes near that gate, because the standing state of the block forbids a third person arriving there carrying shopping, and the woman who does her shopping is in 0768 and nowhere else in the ten. He came with a bare spanner and nothing else when this file was written. The review of 0058 found that a man with a bare spanner cannot also drill the gate's new holes, and that the same spanner cannot be pocketed on one line and lying on the flags on the last, and the bag is the fix. It is a tool bag and it is not shopping, and the prohibition this file wrote is untouched.** All other arrivals are standing figures or figures already on the page before this block. Inside the ceiling of four.
bands.late_twenties_sits_out: The man off the ring road is not in the ten. He may only be written for a second job on the page, in a different room, for a different reason, with the reason in this file. No such job is on the page, so he sits out. He is not any of the three new men and he is not the man from the cottage, and no writer may place him as any of them.

calendar.anchor: 0764 is Thursday the thirteenth of October 2022.
calendar.floor: 0765 may be dated from Sunday the sixteenth of October 2022 by a gap of three to seven, onward three to seven. Thirteen October plus three is the sixteenth and the floor is three days and not two, which is the correction the review of 0057 made in the handoff prompt and which this block takes as settled.
calendar.span_note: Forty-two days counted off two dates, the twenty-fourth of November minus the thirteenth of October. The ten gaps add to the same forty-two and both were counted off the real 2022 calendar and neither was copied out of the other or out of any summary in `state/`, which is the note the review of 0057 left for this block. Ten dates give nine gaps between them plus the incoming gap from 0764, which is why there are ten.
calendar.bound_both_directions: Tight from 0764: ten gaps of three to seven span thirty to seventy days, so Saturday the twelfth of November 2022 to Thursday the twenty-second of December 2022. Loose from the floor of Sunday the sixteenth of October plus nine gaps of twenty-seven to sixty-three: Saturday the twelfth of November 2022 to Sunday the eighteenth of December 2022. The ladder falls at forty-two days on Thursday the twenty-fourth of November and sits inside both pairs, and 0771 stands exactly on the earliest legal date of both.
calendar.weekdays_checked: All ten taken off the real 2022 calendar, twice, and not copied out of any summary. Sunday, Thursday, Tuesday, Saturday, Wednesday, Monday, Saturday, Wednesday, Sunday, Thursday, which is SIX different days among the ten, namely Sunday, Thursday, Tuesday, Saturday, Wednesday and Monday, two of them on a Saturday and two on a Sunday. None on the ninth and none on the eleventh of any month. No two share a date. None before Sunday the sixteenth of October 2022. No chapter spans two dates. **This line was WRONG when first written and was wrong twice, and the review of 0058 is what found it: it printed Tuesday at the eighth position, which is 0772 and is a Wednesday, and it called the ten five different days when they are six. calendar.what_may_not_be_printed: No day tally in body, dateline, opening or closing, and no closed clock time anywhere. What survives is tenure by month and season, age, date, and standing objects.
calendar.note_on_the_card_and_the_prose: Ten dates and ten gaps as above, taken off the real 2022 calendar and not copied out of any summary. Card 0771 calls 0764 'the same shed six weeks earlier in the season' and that is thirty days, and the prose says since October, and the prose wins.

cards.0765: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has four pallets flat on the concrete with the bottom boards gone black, the woman who books work stands them on edge leaning back off the fence with a finger of air between them, and the wet stays in the middle of all four.
cards.0766: At number ten a woman in her early thirties means to dig a muddy path out to the shed and lay gravel in it, her sister lays three boards down the side of the bed along the fall of the path, and every rain runs along them and off the low end into the hollow they were put down to stop.
cards.0767: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight means to shift a barrowful of loose brick off the top of her yard wall, her sister builds it into a proper stack on the two best bricks, and the wall is a brick short at the coping where the frost will get in.
cards.0768: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has firewood gone green at the bottom end, the woman who does her shopping stacks it on end in the coal hole, and the middle of the load goes green and furry and comes out in the spring.
cards.0769: At the unit a man in his early forties has a gate post loose with wire wrapped round it from the top down, the man from the cottage digs it up and wires it top and bottom and leaves the middle free, and the post leans in the middle between the two turns like a hinge.
cards.0770: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a trolley that comes sideways when she pulls it, a man from over the gate takes the caster off and fits a new one and lines it up square, and the new wheel is smaller so the trolley sits low at the front and goes over on the ramp.
cards.0771: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a shed door stile gone soft at the bottom, a man from the end of the row lets in a length of scaffold board and screws it tight, and it stands proud of the face and the beech will move across it in the winter.
cards.0772: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a kitchen floor lifting along the passage door, the woman who does the front steps takes the whole sheet up and lays it back end for end, and its far edge lies over the sill so the door catches on it and the grit comes back in.
cards.0773: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a gate that will not shut square, a man who does odd work up the road hangs it on the other side, and it stands open across the front path with the new screws three threads into the rail.
cards.0774: At the unit a man in his early forties has a vent at the back that has not been cleared since the last lot cleared it, the woman from two doors down fits a cowl over the opening, and the air that used to go out of it comes back in under the door and the back wall of the store takes a damp patch.

movement: Nothing is rescued. The freeholder does not arrive. No plate is unscrewed and no wire is spliced. The ladder is not opened and no room is painted. The box behind the bench is not opened. The drawer with leads and screws is not opened. The drawer at ten stays shut with the hammer, the screwdriver and the paper. The front room at number twelve is not entered. The report is not chased. The envelope is not turned. The bowl stays on its shelf and the ring stays on the tiles. No felt is nailed. No ply is nailed. The gate at twelve stays propped and the coal shed stays shut. The sash at twelve stays a hand's width low. The slab at nine stays tilting to the rail. What moves in the ten is four pallets, three boards, a stack of brick, a stack of firewood, a length of wire, a caster wheel, a length of scaffold board, a sheet of floor, a gate on its hangings and a cowl on a vent, and every one of them is left in the wrong state.
door_meetings: Nobody is kept at a boundary in this block. 0765 the woman who books work in the yard of the lock-up, 0766 a sister through the gate at ten, 0767 a sister at the front door of twelve and round to the back, 0768 the woman who does her shopping in through the front door of nine, 0769 the man from the cottage straight through the gate at the unit, 0770 the man from over the lock-up gate at the roller door, 0771 the man from the end of the row at the back door of ten, 0772 the woman who does the front steps at the back door of twelve, 0773 the man who does odd work up the road at the gate of nine with a canvas tool bag, 0774 the woman from two doors down at the unit gate. The same two people in the same manner happens in no two chapters: the woman who books work is at the rear of the van in 0757, inside the lock-up on the concrete in 0762 and out in the yard in 0765; the man from the cottage is at the unit gate with his hands in front of him in 0761 and straight through it to the post in 0769; the woman who does her shopping leaves her bags on the step all morning in 0758 and takes them straight in in 0768.
closing_images: Ten different ones. Four pallets stood on edge against a fence with a hand under the bottom of the top one. A sack of gravel standing in a shed where it has stood since the spring with the boards laid beside it. A stack of brick built in the corner of a yard with the barrow turned over against the wall beside it. An arm in to the middle of a load of wood and bark coming off it green. A post with two turns of wire on it that moves between them. A trolley that goes forward on the ramp with a load in it and stops with the back legs off the ground. A thumb along an edge of scaffold board standing out of a door stile. A door that stops on a corner of its own floor every time. A gate standing open across a front path. A damp patch coming up the back wall of a store behind a cowl. Only one ending is a thing left where it is, which is the pallet stack in 0765. No ending is a thing put away. The depart-and-do-not-follow gesture appears in only one of the ten, and a departure up a lane in only one of the ten, and those are not the same chapter.

read_back.who: A second reader, given the eight canon chapters 0755, 0756, 0758, 0760, 0761, 0762, 0763 and 0764, the band file and the prompt, and the sixteen points, and asked for arithmetic and facts first and prose last.
read_back.arithmetic_first: Ten findings. The calendar was checked clean off the real 2022 calendar and is not a finding. TWO were arithmetic and both are fixed. 0766 gave the muddy run of the shed path as nine paces and as two yards in the same paragraph while a later paragraph of the same chapter already assumed five firm yards; it now reads five yards firm and the last two of them mud, which is what the card, the dialogue and the caps block all said. 0767 took four coping bricks off a sound run of four feet and then left four feet bare, which is not possible, because four bricks on edge cover about three feet; the sound run at the coal shed end is now seven feet, so four bricks off it leaves four feet bare, and the same paragraph's 'a lump either side of the gap' has become a lump where the lip was and another at the end where the cap was.
read_back.facts: Eight findings. Seven of the eight are good and stand. 0767 had the tools go back IN THE COAL SHED, which is a standing object this block may not open, and the tools now go back on the nails by the shed. 0765 gave one door two ways in, the open half of the doors in the orientation line and the gap in the doors forty lines later with the roller door up; both are now one way. 0773 put a stranger's shopping on the step of number nine with nobody to have brought it, which is the third bag-arrival's trace the standing state was written to stop; the bags are gone and it is her own hands in her pockets. 0773 carried a barrow and an unnamed load to the coal hole, which a reader would take for the wood 0768 left standing green; the trip is now to see whether she shut the lid, and nothing is carried. 0773's caps block said the other side of the posts where the body says the other side of the ledgers, and the body is right, because the fault that ends the chapter is his screws going into the ledger. 0771's caps block gave the fault as the water running across the board into the joint, which is the man's argument against the host's batten and not the fault the body leaves; it now says the board stands proud, the door does not shut against the side of it, and the beech water comes down the face of the door for the rest of the winter. 0770's last sentence had the load off the trolley and the wall and the trolley with a load on it on the ramp in the same sentence; she now puts the load back on and pulls it up again, which is what the declared closing image needs. 0770 also had the only hour in the ten, 'before six', and it now says before the light. **THE EIGHTH IS WITHDRAWN, BECAUSE ITS PREMISE WAS FALSE AND IT DID HARM. It reads, in the version first written: '0765's caps block said four pallets turned over and the body turns three.' The body turned four and turns four still, at lines 15, 17, 19, 33, 69, 79, 97, 101 and 107. The caps block said four and was RIGHT. The repair changed it to three on a false premise, which left one sentence contradicting itself on the line, and the review of 0058 caught that as its first finding. The caps block has been put back to four, the one-word repair is undone, and this entry is left standing as it was written so that the false premise is on the record and not quietly deleted. A finding whose basis is wrong is worse than no finding, and the only honest thing to do with one is to keep it and mark it.**
read_back.prose_last: Four findings. settled_by_this_block.the_reading_of_thing_left_where_it_is: The PROMPT allows at most one ending on a thing put away and at most one on a thing left where it is. The band's declared family requires the one thing the good method cannot do to be left standing at the end of every chapter. Read narrowly and in line with the review of 0057, a THING LEFT WHERE IT IS is an object that was to be moved, worked on or taken away and was not. On that reading only 0766 closes on one, in the sack of gravel at the back of the shed, and nothing in the ten closes on a thing put away. The eight other endings close on a fault the adopted method made in the course of the chapter and nobody undid, which is what the family asks for. This reading is settled here so that a later block does not re-open it, and a later block that wants the fault off the last line may put it off, because nothing in the family forbids that.
